name: Facelift tape (Hollywood facelift)

lead: Facelift tape, sometimes called a Hollywood facelift, uses thin medical-grade tape on the face and neck, attached to strings that are tied behind the head. The strings pull the skin back and up, tightening the jawline and smoothing the cheeks and neck for as long as the tape stays in place.

Makeup artists use the technique before photo shoots, and it is described as a method used by film and television stars for red-carpet events. Dermatology commentary describes the result as temporary and dependent on placement, lighting and how well the cords are hidden.

paras: Tape is placed in discreet spots, often near the hairline or in front of the ear, and a cord is tied behind the head or under the hair to hold the tension. Hair and makeup hide the tape and strings. It is typically used for a single event or shoot rather than daily wear.

The adhesive can irritate skin, clog pores, and cause allergic reactions, painful removal, tearing or scarring, and daily use raises those risks, according to one skincare company's medical review. The effect ends when the tape comes off.

chain: Tape and hidden cords pull skin up and back
Jawline, cheeks and neck look tighter
Temporary lifted look for photos or events
angle.text: While the tape is on, the cords physically hold facial skin in a raised position, giving a tighter-looking jaw and smoother cheeks. Users apply it for photographs, filming or events; the look lasts only as long as the tape stays in place.

lead: Facelift tape, popularly called a Hollywood facelift, is a temporary cosmetic technique in which medical-grade tape is applied to the face or neck and connected to strings tied behind the head, lifting the skin upward.[1] The strings are usually hidden by hair and the tape by makeup.[1]

People use it to look more lifted for a specific moment: makeup artists use it before photo shoots, and Hollywood stars are reported to use it for red-carpet events.[1] The visible effect depends on tape placement, how well the string is concealed and the lighting, and it disappears when the tape is removed.[1]

A related practice, overnight taping of expression lines, went viral on TikTok; a skincare company's article notes that wrinkle patches such as Frownies date to 1889.[1] No clinical trial of facelift taping is known.

paras: Facelift taping places medical tape on the face and neck, attached to strings tied behind the head to pull the skin upward; hair covers the string and makeup covers the tape.[1] Makeup artists use it before photo shoots and it is described as common among stars before red-carpet appearances.[1]

Overnight face taping, in which tape is placed over expression lines during sleep, became a social media trend.[1] The commentary linked here notes that tape does not remove existing wrinkles and that it can make lines look deeper because facial muscles keep trying to move beneath it.[1]

The main concern is the adhesive. Medical-grade tape can still irritate skin, clog pores and contribute to breakouts, and possible complications listed include painful removal, allergic reaction, bleeding, tearing and scarring; daily taping increases the risks.[1]

timeline.event: Frownies, an early wrinkle-patch brand, is dated to this year in one skincare article.[1]
